summary: The study investigates the deposition of thin hafnium oxides using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with HfCl4 and H2O precursors at 350/C176C. The films are analyzed for their composition, oxygen content, and behavior during thermal annealing and oxidation. The results show that the films are under-stoichiometric in oxygen and contain chlorine contamination. The study also examines the exchange of oxygen between the gas phase and the film matrix during thermal oxidation.
evidence: We have deposited thin ﬁlms (3.5, 7.5 and 22 nm) by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using HfCl4 and H2O precursors at 350/C176C. Growth, thermal annealing and thermal reoxidation of the thin hafnium oxide layers under controlled ultra-dry oxygen atmosphere were studied using ion beam techniques and isotopic tracing experiments.
